story_set.letters: Jerry Robinson (sourced) (logo design, see notes); typeset
story_set.first_line: All brand new adventures of The Batman and Robin, the Boy Wonder!
story_set.notes: According to Klein, Robinson was also probably responsible for the revisions to the logo over the next several issues.

story_set.title: Boys! G-Man Outfit
story_set.first_line: Earn this thrilling prize or any of 300 others and make spending money every week, besides!
story_set.synopsis: Ad for winning prizes from the Crowell-Collier Publishing Co., Springfield Ohio.
story_set.notes: Inside front cover. Also includes indicia.

story_set.title: The Legend of the Batman--Who He Is and How He Came to Be!
story_set.first_line: One night some fifteen years ago, Thomas Wayne, his wife and his son were walking home from a movie...
story_set.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (origin) (featured); Joe Chill (villain) (un-named); Martha Wayne (flashback, death); Thomas Wayne (flashback, death)
story_set.synopsis: Bruce Wayne's parents are murdered by a cheap crook, and young Bruce vows to avenge their deaths by warring on all criminals.
story_set.keywords: Crime Alley; pearl necklace; Wayne Manor

story_set.title: The Joker
story_set.first_line: Once again a master criminal stalks the city streets -- a criminal weaving a web of death about him...
story_set.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (featured); The Joker (villain) (introduction); Robin [Dick Grayson] (featured); Henry (radio listener); Henry Claridge (millionaire, death); Mrs. Claridge (Henry's wife); un-named Police Chief; Jay Wilde (death); Judge Drake (death); Otto Drexel (mention only); Brute Nelson (villain, death)
story_set.synopsis: Batman faces a new criminal who succeeds in killing famous men and stealing their prized possessions, leaving them all with a smile on their face.
story_set.notes:
There is an earlier chronological appearance (and origin) of the Joker in Detective Comics (DC, 1937 series) #168 (February 1951).

Robinson verified with Gary Watson in July 2009 that he did some penciling (including the Joker's card on the splash page specifically), in addition to the background inks and lettering he already confirmed.

First appearance of Joker Venom.
story_set.keywords: Batsuit; Claridge Diamond; Cleopatra Necklace; Daily Star; Gotham City; infra-red lamp; Joker venom; New Jersey; Ronkers Ruby; Wayne Manor

story_set.synopsis: Having bought the Bar Q Ranch, Major Bigsbe decides to celebrate by shootin' off his pistols and lands in jail.
story_set.notes: This was the only appearance of this feature.

story_set.title: The Giants of Hugo Strange
story_set.first_line: While an innocent metropolis sleeps little does it realize that huge, terrifying man-monsters shall soon stalk the streets and bring to them havoc and destruction.
story_set.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (featured); Professor Hugo Strange (villain); Monster Men (villains, introduction, all die)
story_set.synopsis: The Batman faces an arch criminal who has invented a serum to create a race of giant monsters and nearly becomes one of them himself.
story_set.notes:
This story was originally prepared for Detective Comics (DC, 1937 series) #38 (April 1940), but with the introduction of Robin in that issue, the story (sans Robin) was published here. 

Oddity: Machine guns are mounted on the Batplane, which are used to kill. 

The closing scenes of Batman battling one of the monsters look as if they were taken directly from 1933's film, "King Kong."

story_set.title: Strictly Publicity
story_set.first_line: 'It just isn't possible!' The Chief was saying.
story_set.synopsis: Detective Terry Gallant proves to his Chief that the late Barton Barlow had killed himself with a gun in a most mysterious way.

story_set.title: Meet the Artist!
story_set.first_line: Readers, meet Bob Kane, creator of The Batman!
story_set.synopsis: Biography of Batman creator, Bob Kane.

story_set.title: The Cat
story_set.first_line: Among the guests walks a young steward... Dick Grayson who is in reality... Robin the Boy Wonder!
story_set.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (featured); The Cat (villain) (disguised as Miss Peggs, introduction, see notes); Robin [Dick Grayson] (featured); John Travers; Martha Travers; Dr. Wallace; un-named ship steward; un-named Captain (of "The Dolphin"); Denny (villain)
story_set.synopsis: Batman and Robin take a trip aboard an exclusive yacht in order to prevent the theft of the Travers necklace at the hands of the Cat.
story_set.notes:
The Cat was later renamed Cat-Woman or Catwoman in the next issue. 

An earlier chronological appearance was in Batman (DC, 1940 series) #52 (April-May 1949) and in The Brave and the Bold (DC, 1955 series) #197 (April 1983).
story_set.keywords: Atlantic Ocean; batrope; breaking the fourth wall; luxury cruise ship; speedboat; Traver's Necklace

story_set.title: The "Big Six" Comics Magazines Still Lead the Field!

story_set.title: Two Aces

story_set.synopsis: Inventor Doctor Synce gets Navy flier Wayne to fly secret plans from Pensacola, Florida to the coast, when the pilot runs up against an old adversary and ace from years before.

story_set.notes: Ginger Snap was previously seen in More Fun Comics #53 (March 1940).

story_set.first_line: In Egypt they say 'How are you sweating?' instead of 'How is your health?'

story_set.notes: The Fantastic Facts feature previously appeared in Adventure Comics #49 (April 1940).

story_set.title: The Joker Returns
story_set.first_line: Once again that harlequin of hate..the Joker..brings grinning death to a terrified people...
story_set.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (featured); Commissioner James Gordon (supporting); Joker (villain); Robin [Dick Grayson] (featured); Chief of Police Chalmers (death); Edgar Martin (a political reformer, death)
story_set.synopsis: The Joker escapes from prison to continue his rampage of death and to steal the famed Cleopatra necklace and Fire Ruby.
story_set.notes:
As recounted in various sources, the Joker was supposed to die of his stab wound at the end of the story, but the editors decided this villain was too good to kill off, so the last panels were re-drawn to show him surviving. 

The last panel of the story, titled "Golden Rules for Robin's Regulars", introduces readers to "Robin's Code" of conduct. The code (ROBIN): Readiness, Obedience, Brotherhood, Industriousness, Nationalism.

This story was apparently intended for Detective Comics (DC, 1937 series) #40 (June 1940). The cover of that issue (shown in a promotional house advertisement in this issue) shows Robin trapped on a flagpole about to be chopped down, which occurs here. The villain also appears to be a recolored Joker.
story_set.keywords: Cleopatra Necklace; Fire Ruby; Joker venom
